question: On a chain of resolved bioelectric cells with Kir2.1, NaV1.2, leaks and gap junctions, does a bistable voltage domain wall form with width scaling as sqrt(G), pin at weak coupling, show hysteresis under a slowly ramped control, and does a written domain return after its tissue is cut and restored?

theory_sources.McNamara 2020: McNamara HM et al., Bioelectrical domain walls in homogeneous tissues, Nat Phys 16:357-364 (2020), PMC8008956: C_m dV/dt = G_cxn lap V - I(V); walls stationary only at the equal-area (Maxwell) balance in a homogeneous tissue, otherwise they migrate to expand the stronger state; width grows as sqrt(G_cxn); hysteresis under a ramped depolarising (CheRiff) conductance, vanishing in well-coupled tissue
theory_sources.Keener 1987: Keener JP, Propagation and its failure in coupled systems of discrete excitable cells, SIAM J Appl Math 47:556-572, doi:10.1137/0147038: on a discrete chain a bistable front is pinned (propagation failure) below a critical coupling that depends on the detuning

world.cell: heredity cell of validation/tissue/surface_pump_v3_fixtures.py (heredity_cells): BETSE-default membrane coefficients, Na leak x0.2, Kir2.1 1e-8 m/s, NaV1.2 2.5e-7 m/s, Na/K-ATPase, held bath per cell, 310 K, fixed volume
world.nav_availability: 0.4 (held). Needed so that a cell without the control is monostable H and a hysteresis loop can close; at full NaV1.2 the D state persists at zero control
world.control: per-cell Na-leak population naleak_always_open@1 with 2e-10 m/s at availability u
world.write: per-cell Na-leak population, 1.92e-9 m/s, on from 0.05 to 0.35 s in written cells
world.junctions: constant_field@1, Na K M permeable (P blocked), area 1e-11 m^2; gate junction_voltage_relaxation@1 held open (minimum open fraction 1, initial 1, threshold 0); permeability set so that G = kappa g_H, g_H the H-state slope conductance
world.initial_state: every cell in the self-consistent slow H state at the Maxwell control u_M (composition = slow H at u_M; fast I-V equal-area at u_M)
world.why_not_kir_plus_leak_alone: Checked (development note): with this Kir2.1 law (m_inf half-point -96.5 mV, slope 23 mV) Kir2.1 plus a Na leak alone is bistable only in a 2.5% window of P_leak/P_Kir, with both states depolarised (-24 and +36 mV); with the default K and anion leaks the window is under 0.2% at P_Kir 1e-6 m/s and absent at 1e-7 m/s or less. McNamara-type bistability here needs the NaV1.2 window current, as the heredity pre-screen found

criteria.basis: the declared H state is stationary in the engine
a written cell settles on the reduced model's fast D (the write loads under 1% Na)
continuum width proportional to sqrt(G) (McNamara 2020); fit over kappa 1, 2, 4, 8; reduced discrete slope 0.520
stationary wall of the same laws; residual differences from gate kinetics are transient and from composition drift small over 6 s
ARS(2,2,2) preserves steady states; 1 and 0.5 ms against 0.25 ms
Keener 1987: below the predicted critical coupling (0.5 G*) the wall stays within half a cell over 20 s
above it (2 G*) the wall moves into H (reduced 5.7 cells)
single-cell bistability gives a hysteresis loop
switching points within two ramp steps of the reduced model under the same ramp (quasi-static gates and fixed composition in the reduced model)
a homogeneous chain in a uniform state evolves as one cell (no junction current)
with a wall present the loop is set by depinning, which narrows as coupling grows (McNamara: hysteresis vanishes in tissue); reduced widths 0.35, 0.15, 0.0
the write produced the declared domain before the cut
no cut: the domain persists; cut without restore: the isolated domain and background keep their states
no domain appears without a write
engine domain matches the reduced model's

The residual was not a per-bath rounding floor: each IMEX step booked the electrode increment by differencing plate charges from two different field solves, which did not telescope; it is now booked from the step's start and end charge states (5ba4426). lead_review.decision: Registered with every criterion as drafted blind. The weaknesses below were found on review. They are recorded rather than repaired, because B4's sign had already been seen in dev-06 before registration and the others need no repair to keep the protocol honest.

known_weaknesses.B4_moves_above: Judged on |shift|; the basis predicts a positive shift (into H). The signed value is saved as engine_shift_cells of the factor-2.0 entry of pinning.cases and reported next to the verdict. A wrong-way move of 2 cells or more would pass B4 but contradict the basis, and would be reported as such.
known_weaknesses.B5_anchored_narrows: Threshold 0 admits equal widths (no narrowing). The registered reduced widths (0.35, 0.15, 0.0) are compared in the unjudged registered-predictions rows. Narrowing is claimed only if the decrements are positive.
known_weaknesses.B6_cut_restore_returns: At kappa 0.25 every cell is bistable and the walls are pinned, so return after cut and restore is close to guaranteed by construction. B6 tests the cut and restore machinery and the conservation across it, not a memory mechanism.
known_weaknesses.B7_charge: Redundant with the engine's own global-charge guard, which refuses a run before the ratio reaches 1. It is kept as a recorded margin.
